title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第17部分：硅

chapters.SIMT: 3. 线程束、分支发散与延迟
chapters.Matmul: 5. 矩阵乘法就是工作负载

5bd5f25b40ae.en: In 2012, the neural network that started the deep learning boom, AlexNet, was trained in five to six days on two graphics cards made for video games. <bookmark mark='a'/> Twelve years later Meta trained Llama 3.1, a language model of 405 billion parameters, on 16,384 of NVIDIA's H100 GPUs: here they are, one square each. <bookmark mark='b'/> By Epoch AI's count, that run used about 81 million times as many floating-point operations as AlexNet. Almost all of them were multiplications and additions of matrices.
5bd5f25b40ae.zh: 2012年，掀起深度学习热潮的那个神经网络AlexNet，是在两块为电子游戏设计的显卡上，训练了五到六天。<bookmark mark='a'/>十二年后，Meta在16384块英伟达H100 GPU上训练了Llama 3.1，一个4050亿参数的语言模型：它们都在这里，一块GPU一个小方格。<bookmark mark='b'/>按Epoch AI的统计，这次训练用掉的浮点运算，大约是AlexNet的8100万倍。其中几乎全部，都是矩阵的乘法和加法。

7d2573fb81eb.en: The computer making this video reports its processor as Intel Xeon Processor. <bookmark mark='a'/> We measured how fast one of its cores multiplies matrices: at best, about 102 billion operations a second. <bookmark mark='b'/> At that speed, AlexNet's training would take about 53 days. <bookmark mark='c'/> Llama 3.1's would take about 12 million years.
7d2573fb81eb.zh: 制作这个视频的计算机，报告它的处理器是Intel Xeon Processor。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们测了它的一个核心做矩阵乘法有多快：最快大约每秒1020亿次运算。<bookmark mark='b'/>照这个速度，AlexNet的训练要花大约53天。<bookmark mark='c'/>Llama 3.1的训练，要花大约1200万年。

4ff8ae8137e5.en: That gap is the subject of this part. Why does AI run on graphics processors, and what would a chip built for it look like? <bookmark mark='a'/> We'll follow the hardware from the moment clock speeds stopped rising, through the GPU, CUDA and AlexNet, to the arithmetic of matrix products and the roofline that bounds them, Google's TPU, numbers four bits wide, and machines the size of a room that act as one computer. <bookmark mark='b'/> And wherever we can, we'll measure it on the computer making this video.
4ff8ae8137e5.zh: 这道鸿沟，就是本部分的主题。为什么人工智能跑在图形处理器上？为它专门造的芯片，又会是什么样子？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会沿着硬件的历史走下去：从时钟频率不再上涨的那一刻，经过GPU、CUDA和AlexNet，到矩阵乘法的算术，以及给它的速度设上限的屋顶线；再到谷歌的TPU、只有四位宽的数字，以及一整间屋子那么大、却像一台计算机一样工作的机器。<bookmark mark='b'/>只要能做到，我们就在制作这个视频的这台计算机上亲手测量。

6542adbceaa4.en: This is Part 17 of AI, Built, in the third act, the transformer era. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: why clocks stopped getting faster; how graphics chips became the engines of AI; why matrix multiplication is the workload, and what bounds its speed, from the memory hierarchy to the roofline; systolic arrays and the number formats in the hardware; how chips talk to each other; how a fast kernel is written; and where the hardware stands now.
6542adbceaa4.zh: 这是《人工智能，从零搭建》的第17部分，属于第三幕：Transformer时代。<bookmark mark='a'/>本部分要讲：时钟为什么不再变快；图形芯片怎样变成了人工智能的发动机；为什么矩阵乘法就是工作负载，又是什么限制了它的速度，从存储层次一直讲到屋顶线；脉动阵列，以及硬件里的数字格式；芯片之间怎样通信；快速的内核是怎样写出来的；以及今天的硬件走到了哪一步。

deebf9e28d99.en: In 1965 Gordon Moore, then at Fairchild Semiconductor, noticed that the number of components on a chip had been doubling every year, and guessed it would keep going. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are fifty years of microprocessors, on a log scale: from Intel's 4004 in 1971, with about 2,300 transistors, to chips with 58 billion. <bookmark mark='b'/> A straight line on a log scale is exponential growth. The fit doubles every 2.0 years, the pace Moore settled on in 1975. For three decades, each doubling also made every program faster, for free.
deebf9e28d99.zh: 1965年，当时在仙童半导体的戈登·摩尔注意到，一块芯片上的元件数一直在逐年翻倍，他猜这会继续下去。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是五十年来的微处理器，画在对数刻度上：从1971年英特尔的4004，大约2300个晶体管，到拥有580亿个晶体管的芯片。<bookmark mark='b'/>对数刻度上的一条直线，就是指数增长。拟合出来是每2.0年翻一倍，正是摩尔在1975年修正后的速度。在三十年里，每一次翻倍也让每个程序免费变快。

a1f1dd499f45.en: Why did shrinking make computers faster? The answer came in 1974 from Robert Dennard and his colleagues at IBM, the engineer who had invented the one-transistor memory cell. <bookmark mark='a'/> Shrink every length of a transistor by a factor kappa, and lower the voltage by the same factor. <bookmark mark='b'/> The capacitance it has to charge falls by kappa, <bookmark mark='c'/> and it switches kappa times faster. <bookmark mark='d'/> The power to switch it is C V squared f, which falls by kappa squared. <bookmark mark='e'/> But kappa squared more transistors now fit in the same area. So the power per square millimetre stays the same, while the clock gets faster and the count goes up. That's Dennard scaling, and for thirty years it was the free lunch.
a1f1dd499f45.zh: 为什么把晶体管做小，计算机就变快？答案在1974年来自IBM的罗伯特·登纳德和同事，他也是单晶体管存储单元的发明者。<bookmark mark='a'/>把晶体管的每个尺寸都缩小κ倍，电压也降低同样的倍数。<bookmark mark='b'/>它要充电的电容降为κ分之一，<bookmark mark='c'/>开关速度快κ倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>开关一次的功耗是C乘V的平方乘f，降为κ平方分之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>但同样的面积现在能放下κ平方倍的晶体管。于是每平方毫米的功耗保持不变，而时钟更快、数量更多。这就是登纳德缩放，三十年里，它就是那顿免费的午餐。

ccf99704cb28.en: Then, in the early two thousands, the voltage stopped falling. <bookmark mark='a'/> A transistor is a switch, and below a certain voltage it can't switch off cleanly: at room temperature the current falls at most tenfold for every sixty millivolts, so a lower voltage means leakage. <bookmark mark='b'/> With the voltage stuck, each smaller transistor uses as much power as the old one, <bookmark mark='c'/> and packing kappa squared more of them into the same area multiplies the heat by kappa squared. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2004 Intel cancelled the successor to the Pentium 4 and turned to two cores per chip. A year later the programmer Herb Sutter wrote that the free lunch was over.
ccf99704cb28.zh: 后来，到了2000年代初，电压降不下去了。<bookmark mark='a'/>晶体管是个开关，电压低于某个值，它就关不干净：在室温下，电压每降60毫伏，电流最多只能降到十分之一，所以电压越低，漏电越多。<bookmark mark='b'/>电压卡住了，每个更小的晶体管，用的功率就和原来一样多，<bookmark mark='c'/>而在同样面积里塞进κ平方倍的晶体管，发热也就乘上了κ平方。<bookmark mark='d'/>2004年，英特尔取消了奔腾4的后继型号，转向每块芯片两个核心。一年后，程序员赫布·萨特写道：免费的午餐结束了。

12154e38a77b.en: You can see the wall in the data. <bookmark mark='a'/> Clock speed doubled every 2.4 years from 1985 to 2003, and stopped near 3.7 gigahertz; and since 2006 it has drifted down by about 1 percent a year. <bookmark mark='b'/> Power had been climbing with it, and it levelled off at what a fan and a heat sink can carry away, around a hundred watts. <bookmark mark='c'/> Single-thread speed, what one program gets, doubled every 1.8 years until then; since 2010, every 6.5. <bookmark mark='d'/> What kept growing was the number of cores. The transistors kept coming; the only way left to use them was in parallel.
12154e38a77b.zh: 这堵墙在数据里看得见。<bookmark mark='a'/>从1985年到2003年，时钟频率每2.4年翻一倍，然后停在了3.7吉赫兹左右；从2006年起，它每年还下降了大约1%。<bookmark mark='b'/>功耗一直跟着上涨，最后停在一个风扇加散热片能带走的水平，大约一百瓦。<bookmark mark='c'/>单线程性能，也就是一个程序能拿到的速度，在那之前每1.8年翻一倍；2010年以后，要6.5年。<bookmark mark='d'/>一直在增长的，是核心的数量。晶体管还在不断增加；剩下唯一能用上它们的办法，就是并行。

2e8bba44898d.en: Why does parallel win? <bookmark mark='a'/> Switching power is C V squared f, and to run a clock faster you have to raise the voltage roughly in proportion. So power grows like the cube of the clock. <bookmark mark='b'/> To do twice the work, one core at twice the clock burns about eight times the power. Two cores at the same clock burn twice the power. <bookmark mark='c'/> The catch is Amdahl's law, from 1967: the part of a program that can't be split limits the speed-up, however many cores you add. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the winning chip for a problem that splits into millions of identical pieces has thousands of slow, simple lanes. That chip already existed. It drew video games.
2e8bba44898d.zh: 为什么并行能赢？<bookmark mark='a'/>开关功耗是C乘V的平方乘f，而要让时钟跑得更快，电压大致要成比例地提高。所以功耗随时钟频率的三次方增长。<bookmark mark='b'/>要做两倍的工作，一个核心把时钟提高一倍，功耗大约是八倍；两个核心保持原来的时钟，功耗只是两倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是1967年的阿姆达尔定律：程序里不能拆开的那部分，限制了加速比，不管你加多少核心。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，对一个能拆成几百万个相同小块的问题，最好的芯片，是成千上万条又慢又简单的通道。这样的芯片已经存在了。它是用来画电子游戏的。

2287c45d9e3a.en: Chapter two. From pixels to GPGPU.
2287c45d9e3a.zh: 第2章。从像素到GPU通用计算。

d38cedcfda22.en: Think about what a graphics card does. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every pixel on the screen runs the same small program, a shader, on its own coordinates, and no pixel needs to know about any other. <bookmark mark='b'/> A 1080p screen is about two million pixels, sixty times a second: over a hundred million runs of the same program every second, all independent. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1999 NVIDIA sold the GeForce 256 as the world's first GPU, a graphics processing unit, and in 2001 its shaders became programmable. It was a chip built for doing one thing an enormous number of times.
d38cedcfda22.zh: 想想显卡是做什么的。<bookmark mark='a'/>屏幕上每个像素，都在自己的坐标上运行同一个小程序，叫着色器，而且没有哪个像素需要知道别的像素。<bookmark mark='b'/>一块1080p的屏幕大约有两百万个像素，每秒六十次：每秒超过一亿次运行同一个程序，彼此完全独立。<bookmark mark='c'/>1999年，英伟达把GeForce 256作为世界上第一块GPU，也就是图形处理器来卖；2001年，它的着色器变得可以编程。这是一块为“把一件事做极多次”而造的芯片。

ead27bf0bc1f.en: A CPU and a GPU spend their transistors differently. <bookmark mark='a'/> A CPU spends them on making one stream of instructions fast: large caches, so data is close; branch predictors that guess which way the program will go; machinery to run instructions out of order. <bookmark mark='b'/> A GPU spends them on arithmetic: many small processors, NVIDIA calls them streaming multiprocessors, each a block of simple lanes. <bookmark mark='c'/> The computer making this video has 4 cores, each with vector units 16 numbers wide. An H100 has 132 streaming multiprocessors with 128 lanes each: almost seventeen thousand. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each lane is slow and simple. There are just a great many of them.
ead27bf0bc1f.zh: CPU和GPU，把晶体管花在了不同的地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>CPU把它们花在让一条指令流跑得快上：大缓存，让数据离得近；分支预测器，猜程序会往哪边走；还有让指令乱序执行的机制。<bookmark mark='b'/>GPU把它们花在算术上：许多小处理器，英伟达叫它们流式多处理器，每个都是一组简单的通道。<bookmark mark='c'/>制作这个视频的计算机有4个核心，每个核心的向量单元是16个数宽。一块H100有132个流式多处理器，每个有128条通道：差不多一万七千条。<bookmark mark='d'/>每条通道都又慢又简单。只是数量极多。

536f3682bf06.en: Simple lanes are the easy part. The hard part is feeding them, because memory is far away. <bookmark mark='a'/> There's a law from queueing theory, John Little's, from 1961: the number of things in a system equals the rate they arrive times how long each one stays. <bookmark mark='b'/> For memory, it says: to keep a memory busy, the bytes you have asked for but not yet received must equal the bandwidth times the latency. <bookmark mark='c'/> Researchers measured a Hopper GPU's memory at about 270 nanoseconds away. At two terabytes a second, it needs about 560 kilobytes on the way at every moment: thousands of requests. <bookmark mark='d'/> One core of this computer, measured, needs only about 48 cache lines on the way, and it gets them from prefetchers that guess the next addresses of a long, regular read. A GPU gets its thousands the other way: from thousands of threads, each waiting on its own load.
536f3682bf06.zh: 简单的通道是容易的部分。难的是喂饱它们，因为内存离得很远。<bookmark mark='a'/>排队论里有一条定律，是约翰·利特尔1961年提出的：系统里的东西的数量，等于它们到达的速率，乘以每个停留的时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>用在内存上，它说的是：要让内存一直忙着，已经请求、还没收到的字节数，必须等于带宽乘以延迟。<bookmark mark='c'/>研究人员测得，Hopper GPU的内存大约在270纳秒之外。每秒两太字节，就需要每时每刻大约有560千字节在路上：成千上万个请求。<bookmark mark='d'/>这台计算机的一个核心，实测只需要大约48个缓存行在路上，它靠预取器来做到：预取器会猜一段长而规则的读取接下来的地址。GPU用另一种办法凑出那成千上万个请求：成千上万个线程，每个都在等自己的那次读取。

86007b1c6bdd.en: Researchers noticed. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the early two thousands they disguised arithmetic as graphics: store an array as a texture, write the computation as a pixel shader, and read the answer back from the screen. Ian Buck's Brook language at Stanford, in 2004, made that bearable. <bookmark mark='b'/> The same year, Kyoung-Su Oh and Keechul Jung ran a neural network on a graphics card, twenty times faster than on the CPU. <bookmark mark='c'/> Buck went to NVIDIA, and with John Nickolls built CUDA: plain C, plus a way to launch a function on thousands of threads at once. It was announced with the GeForce 8800 in November 2006 and released in 2007. <bookmark mark='d'/> By 2009 Rajat Raina, Anand Madhavan and Andrew Ng at Stanford trained deep networks on a GPU up to seventy times faster than on a CPU. The pieces of the next decade were on the table.
86007b1c6bdd.zh: 研究人员注意到了。<bookmark mark='a'/>在2000年代初，他们把算术伪装成图形：把数组存成纹理，把计算写成像素着色器，再从屏幕上把答案读回来。2004年，伊恩·巴克在斯坦福做的Brook语言，让这件事变得可以忍受。<bookmark mark='b'/>同一年，吴京洙和郑基哲在显卡上跑了一个神经网络，比在CPU上快二十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>巴克去了英伟达，和约翰·尼科尔斯一起做出了CUDA：就是C语言，外加一种一次在成千上万个线程上启动同一个函数的办法。它在2006年11月随GeForce 8800发布，2007年正式推出。<bookmark mark='d'/>到了2009年，斯坦福的拉贾特·雷纳、阿南德·马达万和吴恩达，在GPU上训练深度网络，比在CPU上快多达七十倍。下一个十年的拼图，已经摆在了桌上。

54fbd3e44916.en: Chapter three. Warps, divergence and latency.
54fbd3e44916.zh: 第3章。线程束、分支发散与延迟。

0b8c0b8a5c8b.en: Here is a CUDA program. <bookmark mark='a'/> The function, a kernel, says what one thread does: work out which element is mine from my block number and my thread number, and update that element. <bookmark mark='b'/> The launch asks for enough blocks of 256 threads to cover the array: for a million elements, about four thousand blocks. <bookmark mark='c'/> The hardware hands blocks to streaming multiprocessors, and splits each block into warps of thirty-two threads. <bookmark mark='d'/> The thirty-two threads of a warp execute the same instruction at the same moment, each on its own data. NVIDIA calls it SIMT, single instruction, multiple threads: a vector machine that you program one thread at a time.
0b8c0b8a5c8b.zh: 这是一个CUDA程序。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个函数叫内核，它说的是一个线程要做什么：根据我的块编号和线程编号，算出哪个元素归我，然后更新这个元素。<bookmark mark='b'/>启动时，要求足够多的、每块256个线程的线程块，来覆盖整个数组：一百万个元素，大约四千个块。<bookmark mark='c'/>硬件把线程块分给流式多处理器，再把每个块切成32个线程一组的线程束。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个线程束的32个线程，在同一时刻执行同一条指令，各自处理自己的数据。英伟达把这叫作SIMT，单指令多线程：一台向量机器，你却是一次一个线程地给它编程。

38d08432b120.en: Lockstep has a price. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose the threads of a warp reach an if, and some take it and some don't. <bookmark mark='b'/> The warp can only issue one instruction at a time, so it runs the if-branch with the other threads masked off, <bookmark mark='c'/> then the else-branch with the first group masked off. Both paths cost the whole warp. That's divergence. <bookmark mark='d'/> We simulated a branch on data across four thousand warps. Random data diverges in almost every warp, and the warp does about 50 percent useful work. Sort the data first, so that neighbours agree, and only the warps at the boundary split.
38d08432b120.zh: 步调一致是有代价的。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设一个线程束里的线程遇到一个if，有的进去，有的不进去。<bookmark mark='b'/>线程束一次只能发一条指令，所以它先执行if分支，把其他线程屏蔽掉，<bookmark mark='c'/>再执行else分支，把第一组屏蔽掉。两条路径都要花掉整个线程束的时间。这就是分支发散。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们在四千个线程束上，模拟了一个依赖数据的分支。随机数据几乎在每个线程束里都会发散，线程束只有大约50%的有用功。先把数据排好序，让相邻的线程意见一致，就只有处在边界上的那几个线程束会分叉。

5d6673bf10da.en: Now the reason for all those threads. A load from memory takes hundreds of cycles; while a warp waits, the scheduler issues instructions from another warp that's ready. <bookmark mark='a'/> We simulated one scheduler with memory 479 cycles away, the latency measured on a Hopper GPU. <bookmark mark='b'/> If each warp does only four operations per load, even sixteen warps keep it busy just 17 percent of the time. <bookmark mark='c'/> With sixty-four operations per load, 9 warps are enough. <bookmark mark='d'/> The lines are Little's law: you need the latency plus the work, divided by the work, warps in flight. An H100's multiprocessor has four schedulers and room for sixty-four warps. Past that, the only way to hide latency is more arithmetic per byte, an idea that comes back in chapter five.
5d6673bf10da.zh: 现在说说为什么要那么多线程。从内存读一次要几百个周期；一个线程束在等的时候，调度器就去发另一个已经就绪的线程束的指令。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们模拟了一个调度器，内存在479个周期之外，这是在一块Hopper GPU上测得的延迟。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每个线程束每次读取只做四次运算，即使有十六个线程束，调度器也只有17%的时间在忙。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果每次读取做六十四次运算，9个线程束就够了。<bookmark mark='d'/>那几条线就是利特尔定律：需要在路上的线程束数，等于延迟加上工作量，再除以工作量。H100的一个多处理器有四个调度器，能容纳六十四个线程束。超过这个数，隐藏延迟的唯一办法，就是每个字节做更多的算术，这个想法在第5章还会出现。

86083820010e.en: One more rule of the road. <bookmark mark='a'/> Memory is read in segments of 128 bytes. When the thirty-two threads of a warp read thirty-two neighbouring numbers, the hardware combines them into one transaction: the loads are coalesced. <bookmark mark='b'/> When they read scattered addresses, the same thirty-two numbers cost many transactions, and most of every segment fetched is thrown away. It's the same lesson as a CPU's cache lines, and it will matter for matrices: walk them along the rows.
86083820010e.zh: 还有一条交通规则。<bookmark mark='a'/>内存是按128字节一段来读的。当一个线程束的32个线程读32个相邻的数，硬件会把它们合成一次传输：这叫访存合并。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果它们读的是分散的地址，同样32个数要花很多次传输，取回来的每一段，大部分都被扔掉了。这和CPU缓存行的道理一样，对矩阵也很重要：要沿着行去走。

b0371f88dd0e.zh: 第4章。AlexNet：深度学习从此改变的那一刻。

63faa5a4be65.en: By 2012 the ingredients were in place. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2009 Fei-Fei Li's group had published ImageNet, millions of labelled photographs, and from 2010 there was a yearly contest: a model sees an image and names it, out of a thousand classes, with five guesses. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2012 a network from Geoffrey Hinton's lab in Toronto, built by Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever, <bookmark mark='c'/> missed on 15.3 percent of the test images. The next best entry missed on 26.2 percent. Nobody had seen a gap like that.
63faa5a4be65.zh: 到2012年，各样原料都备齐了。<bookmark mark='a'/>2009年，李飞飞的团队发布了ImageNet，几百万张标注好的照片；从2010年起，每年有一场比赛：模型看一张图，从一千个类别里说出它是什么，可以猜五次。<bookmark mark='b'/>2012年，多伦多杰弗里·辛顿实验室的一个网络，由亚历克斯·克里热夫斯基和伊利亚·苏茨克维搭建，<bookmark mark='c'/>在15.3%的测试图片上答错。第二名答错了26.2%。谁也没见过这么大的差距。

3fa22e58c09f.en: What made it possible was two gaming graphics cards. <bookmark mark='a'/> The network had sixty million parameters, and one GeForce GTX 580, with three gigabytes of memory, couldn't hold it while training. So Krizhevsky split it: half the filters of each layer on one card, half on the other. <bookmark mark='b'/> The two halves exchange their results only at a few layers, to keep the traffic between the cards small. <bookmark mark='c'/> He wrote the convolutions himself, in CUDA, in a library called cuda-convnet. Training took five to six days, for ninety passes over the 1.2 million images.
3fa22e58c09f.zh: 让这件事成为可能的，是两块游戏显卡。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个网络有六千万个参数，一块3GB显存的GeForce GTX 580，训练时装不下它。于是克里热夫斯基把它一分为二：每一层的卷积核，一半放在一块卡上，一半放在另一块上。<bookmark mark='b'/>两半只在少数几层交换结果，好让两块卡之间的通信量小一些。<bookmark mark='c'/>卷积是他自己用CUDA写的，写在一个叫cuda-convnet的库里。训练花了五到六天，把120万张图片过了九十遍。

47dd82ea4774.en: How much arithmetic was that? <bookmark mark='a'/> About 1.2 million images, times ninety passes, times three quarters of a billion multiply-adds per image, times two operations each, times three, for the backward pass: <bookmark mark='b'/> about 4.9 times ten to the seventeen floating-point operations; the published estimate is 4.7. <bookmark mark='c'/> The two cards could do about 1.5 times ten to the eighteen in five and a half days, so the network kept them about 31 percent busy. <bookmark mark='d'/> On the computer rendering this video, at the best speed we measured, one core would take about 53 days. All 4 cores together should do better, but other jobs were using them when we measured, and together they were no faster than one.
47dd82ea4774.zh: 那是多少算术？<bookmark mark='a'/>大约120万张图片，乘以九十遍，乘以每张图四分之三个十亿次乘加，每次乘加算两次运算，再乘以三，算上反向传播：<bookmark mark='b'/>大约4.9乘以10的17次方次浮点运算；公开的估计是4.7。<bookmark mark='c'/>两块卡在五天半里能做大约1.5乘以10的18次方次，所以这个网络让它们大约31%的时间在忙。<bookmark mark='d'/>在渲染这个视频的计算机上，按我们测到的最快速度，一个核心要大约53天。全部4个核心一起本该更快，但我们测量时别的任务正在用它们，结果一起算也不比一个核心快。

bbee8ff76256.en: After 2012 the field moved onto GPUs. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2014 NVIDIA released cuDNN, a library of deep-learning kernels, so researchers no longer had to write their own. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2016 it built a server around eight GPUs, the DGX-1, and Jensen Huang delivered the first one to OpenAI himself. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2018 Dario Amodei and Danny Hernandez measured the trend: from AlexNet on, the compute in the largest training runs had doubled every 3.4 months, three hundred thousand times in six years. <bookmark mark='d'/> And in 2020 Sara Hooker gave the history a name: the hardware lottery. Ideas succeed when they suit the hardware of their day, and neural networks, all multiply-adds, had drawn a winning ticket, made for video games.
bbee8ff76256.zh: 2012年以后，整个领域搬到了GPU上。<bookmark mark='a'/>2014年，英伟达发布了cuDNN，一个深度学习内核库，研究人员不用再自己写了。<bookmark mark='b'/>2016年，它围绕八块GPU造了一台服务器，DGX-1，黄仁勋亲手把第一台送到了OpenAI。<bookmark mark='c'/>2018年，达里奥·阿莫代伊和丹尼·埃尔南德斯测量了这个趋势：从AlexNet开始，最大规模训练所用的算力每3.4个月翻一倍，六年里增长了三十万倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>2020年，萨拉·胡克给这段历史起了个名字：硬件彩票。一个想法能不能成功，要看它适不适合当时的硬件；神经网络全是乘加，抽中了一张为电子游戏印的中奖彩票。

628770c331a4.en: Chapter five. Matrix multiply is the workload.
628770c331a4.zh: 第5章。矩阵乘法就是工作负载。

fcdc007efc5d.en: Why are GPUs so good for neural networks in particular? Because almost all of a network's arithmetic is one operation. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take GPT-3. For every token, each of its 175 billion weights is used in one multiply and one add: two operations per weight, all of them in matrix products. <bookmark mark='b'/> Attention's own products, queries against keys, add 1.4 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Everything else, the normalizations, the activations, the softmax, is a rounding error, even counted generously. <bookmark mark='d'/> Training does the forward pass and a backward pass twice as expensive: six operations per weight per token. Six times 175 billion parameters times 300 billion tokens gives GPT-3's published compute, to within a fraction of a percent. To make AI faster, make matrix multiplication faster.
fcdc007efc5d.zh: 为什么GPU特别适合神经网络？因为一个网络几乎所有的算术，都是同一种运算。<bookmark mark='a'/>以GPT-3为例。每处理一个词元，它的1750亿个权重，每个都参与一次乘法和一次加法：每个权重两次运算，全部在矩阵乘法里。<bookmark mark='b'/>注意力自己的乘积，也就是查询对键，再加上1.4%。<bookmark mark='c'/>其余的一切，归一化、激活函数、softmax，即使往宽里算，也只是个零头。<bookmark mark='d'/>训练要做一次前向，再做一次代价是它两倍的反向：每个词元每个权重六次运算。6乘以1750亿参数，再乘以3000亿个词元，就得到GPT-3公开的算力，误差不到百分之一。要让人工智能更快，就让矩阵乘法更快。

7d90064deb8b.en: So let's count. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each entry of C is a row of A dotted with a column of B. <bookmark mark='b'/> With K terms, that's K multiplies and K minus one adds: about 2K operations. <bookmark mark='c'/> There are M times N entries, so the whole product costs 2MNK floating-point operations. For square matrices of size n: 2 n cubed. Double the size, eight times the work.
7d90064deb8b.zh: 那就来数一数。<bookmark mark='a'/>C的每个元素，是A的一行和B的一列的点积。<bookmark mark='b'/>有K项，就是K次乘法和K减1次加法：大约2K次运算。<bookmark mark='c'/>一共有M乘N个元素，所以整个乘积要2MNK次浮点运算。对于大小为n的方阵：2n的立方。尺寸翻倍，工作量变成八倍。

4edb1cc36563.en: The arithmetic is only half the cost. The numbers have to come from memory. <bookmark mark='a'/> The ratio of operations to bytes moved is called the arithmetic intensity. <bookmark mark='b'/> Done naively, every multiply-add fetches its two numbers, four bytes each in single precision: two operations for eight bytes, a quarter of an operation per byte. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the whole product only needs A and B read once and C written once: three n squared numbers for 2 n cubed operations. The intensity grows like n over six. <bookmark mark='d'/> For n of a thousand and twenty-four, that's about 170 operations per byte. Each number is used a thousand times. The whole game is to use it a thousand times while it's close by, instead of fetching it a thousand times.
4edb1cc36563.zh: 算术只是一半的代价。数字还得从内存里来。<bookmark mark='a'/>运算次数和搬运字节数之比，叫作算术强度。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果天真地做，每次乘加都去取它的两个数，单精度下每个四字节：八个字节做两次运算，每字节四分之一次运算。<bookmark mark='c'/>可整个乘积只需要把A和B各读一次、C写一次：3n平方个数，做2n立方次运算。算术强度像n除以6那样增长。<bookmark mark='d'/>n等于1024时，大约是每字节170次运算。每个数被用了上千次。整个游戏的关键，就是趁它就在手边，把它用上一千次，而不是去取它一千次。

d0b08aad8337.en: That's what tiling does. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cut C into b by b tiles. To compute one tile, walk along a strip of A and a strip of B, one b by b tile of each at a time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Bring the two tiles into fast memory, multiply them, add into the tile of C, and move on. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every number brought in is used b times, so the intensity is b over four bytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> The limit is the fast memory: three tiles have to fit. Bigger fast memory, bigger tiles, more reuse. <bookmark mark='e'/> In 1981 Hong Jia-Wei and H. T. Kung proved that no schedule can do much better: any way of computing the product moves at least on the order of n cubed over the square root of the fast memory's size.
d0b08aad8337.zh: 这就是分块要做的事。<bookmark mark='a'/>把C切成b乘b的块。要算其中一块，就沿着A的一条和B的一条走，每次各取一个b乘b的块。<bookmark mark='b'/>把这两块搬进快速存储，相乘，加到C的那一块上，然后往下走。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个搬进来的数被用了b次，所以算术强度是b除以4字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>上限在于快速存储：三个块必须放得下。快速存储越大，块越大，复用越多。<bookmark mark='e'/>1981年，洪加威和孔祥重证明，没有哪种顺序能好得多：任何计算这个乘积的方法，搬运的数据量至少是n立方除以快速存储大小的平方根这个量级。

bafbc60b0388.en: We measured this on one core of this computer, multiplying two matrices of size 1,024 in C. <bookmark mark='a'/> The textbook triple loop: 0.43 billion operations a second. It walks down the columns of B, one cache line per number. <bookmark mark='b'/> The same arithmetic with the loops reordered, so every inner loop walks along rows: 12. <bookmark mark='c'/> Tiled: 18, 41 times the textbook loop. <bookmark mark='d'/> The best tile size was 256: three 256 by 256 tiles take 768 kilobytes, which fits in the 1024-kilobyte second-level cache. Past that, the tiles spill out and the speed falls. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the BLAS library numpy calls, tuned by experts, with tiles inside tiles and hand-written vector code: 92, 212 times the textbook loop, for exactly the same arithmetic.
bafbc60b0388.zh: 我们在这台计算机的一个核心上，把两个1024阶的矩阵相乘，测了一下，用的是C语言。<bookmark mark='a'/>教科书上的三重循环：每秒0.43千兆次运算。它沿着B的列往下走，每取一个数就要一条缓存行。<bookmark mark='b'/>同样的算术，换一下循环的顺序，让每个内层循环都沿着行走：12。<bookmark mark='c'/>分块之后：18，是教科书循环的41倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>最好的块大小是256：三个256乘256的块占768千字节，正好放得进1024千字节的二级缓存。再大，块就装不下了，速度随之下降。<bookmark mark='e'/>numpy调用的BLAS库，由专家调优，块里套块，还有手写的向量代码：92，是教科书循环的212倍，算术一模一样。

c69c96639006.en: A GPU's memory is not one thing. Let's zoom in on an H100. <bookmark mark='a'/> Around the chip sit stacks of high-bandwidth memory, DRAM dies piled on top of each other: 80 gigabytes, read at 3.35 terabytes a second, but hundreds of cycles away. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the chip itself, a level-two cache of fifty megabytes, shared by all 132 streaming multiprocessors, about half as far. <bookmark mark='c'/> Inside each multiprocessor: 256 kilobytes of shared memory, which the programmer fills on purpose, about forty cycles away; <bookmark mark='d'/> and the registers, another 256 kilobytes, right next to the arithmetic, read every cycle. Each step down is smaller and closer, and much faster to read.
c69c96639006.zh: GPU的内存不是一样东西。我们放大来看一块H100。<bookmark mark='a'/>芯片周围是一叠叠高带宽内存，DRAM裸片一层层摞起来：80GB，每秒能读3.35太字节，但远在几百个周期之外。<bookmark mark='b'/>芯片本身上，有五十兆字节的二级缓存，由全部132个流式多处理器共用，距离大约是一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个多处理器里面：256千字节的共享内存，由程序员有意地去填，大约四十个周期远；<bookmark mark='d'/>还有寄存器，又是256千字节，紧挨着运算单元，每个周期都能读。每往下一层，就更小、更近，读起来也快得多。

a6ab681d03ea.en: That memory is a feat of its own. <bookmark mark='a'/> High-bandwidth memory stacks DRAM dies on top of each other, wired straight through the silicon, and sets the stack right beside the GPU on a slab of silicon with thousands of short wires: far more of them than a circuit board could carry. AMD first used it in a graphics card in 2015. <bookmark mark='b'/> Since the P100, the memory per GPU has grown from 16 gigabytes to 288 for Rubin, and its bandwidth from 0.73 terabytes a second to 19.2: about 26 times in ten years. It's the most expensive part of the package, and, as we'll see, the scarcest resource.
a6ab681d03ea.zh: 那种内存本身就是一项壮举。<bookmark mark='a'/>高带宽内存把DRAM裸片一层层叠起来，用直接穿过硅片的导线连通，再把整叠内存放在GPU旁边的一块硅片上，用成千上万根短导线相连：比电路板能承载的多得多。AMD在2015年第一次把它用在显卡上。<bookmark mark='b'/>从P100开始，每块GPU的内存从16GB增长到Rubin的288GB，带宽从每秒0.73太字节增长到19.2：十年里大约26倍。它是整个封装里最贵的部分，而且我们会看到，也是最稀缺的资源。

0e6ffe1b55f7.en: We can see the same hierarchy on this computer's own processor, by timing it. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the left, one core reads an array over and over and adds it up; the array grows from four kilobytes to 256 megabytes. While it fits in the first-level cache, about 182 gigabytes a second. Past that, from the second level, about 98. From main memory, about 9. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the right, the same core follows a chain of pointers in random order, so every read waits for the one before. In the first-level cache, a read takes about 1.6 nanoseconds; in the second, about 5; in main memory, about 190. <bookmark mark='c'/> The dashed lines are the cache sizes the processor reports. The last level is nominally 33 megabytes, but it's shared by every core on the chip, and here our walk leaves it after about 4.
0e6ffe1b55f7.zh: 在这台计算机自己的处理器上，计个时，也能看到同样的层次。<bookmark mark='a'/>左边，一个核心反复读一个数组，把它加起来；数组从四千字节增大到256兆字节。它还放得进一级缓存时，大约每秒182GB。超出以后，从二级缓存读，大约98。从主存读，大约9。<bookmark mark='b'/>右边，同一个核心按随机顺序追着一串指针走，所以每次读都要等上一次读完。在一级缓存里，一次读大约1.6纳秒；在二级缓存里，大约5；在主存里，大约190。<bookmark mark='c'/>虚线是处理器报告的各级缓存大小。最后一级缓存名义上有33兆字节，但它由芯片上所有核心共用，在这里我们的随机读取大约到4兆字节就离开了它。

e2f0d6f5d44c.en: Why build it this way? Distance costs energy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Mark Horowitz tabulated what each operation costs on a 45-nanometre chip. Adding two 32-bit numbers: a tenth of a picojoule. Multiplying two floats: 3.7. <bookmark mark='b'/> Reading 32 bits from a small on-chip memory: about five. <bookmark mark='c'/> Reading them from DRAM: 640, as much as about 173 multiplies. The arithmetic is cheap; moving the numbers is what costs. The newer chips change the numbers, not the ratio's lesson: every byte fetched from far away has to be used many times.
e2f0d6f5d44c.zh: 为什么要这样造？因为距离要耗能。<bookmark mark='a'/>马克·霍洛维茨列出了在45纳米芯片上，每种操作的代价。两个32位整数相加：十分之一皮焦。两个浮点数相乘：3.7。<bookmark mark='b'/>从一小块片上存储读32位：大约5。<bookmark mark='c'/>从DRAM读：640，相当于大约173次乘法。算术很便宜；搬运数字才是贵的。新的芯片改变了这些数字，却没改变这个比值的教训：每个从远处取来的字节，都必须用上很多次。

0a5f5fd77d20.en: Chapters two to six give a program two ways to be slow. <bookmark mark='a'/> If it does W operations on a machine whose peak is P operations a second, it takes at least W over P. <bookmark mark='b'/> If it moves Q bytes through a memory of bandwidth beta, it takes at least Q over beta. <bookmark mark='c'/> It can't beat either, so its speed, W over T, is at most the smaller of P and beta times W over Q. <bookmark mark='d'/> W over Q is the arithmetic intensity, I: operations per byte. So the speed is at most the minimum of P and beta times I. In 2009 Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman and David Patterson at Berkeley drew this as a picture, and called it the roofline.
0a5f5fd77d20.zh: 第2到第6章，给了一个程序两种慢下来的方式。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果它要做W次运算，机器的峰值是每秒P次，那至少要W除以P的时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果它要通过带宽为β的内存搬运Q个字节，那至少要Q除以β的时间。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个都快不过，所以它的速度，W除以T，至多是P和β乘以W除以Q中较小的那个。<bookmark mark='d'/>W除以Q就是算术强度I：每字节的运算次数。所以速度至多是P和β乘以I的最小值。2009年，伯克利的塞缪尔·威廉斯、安德鲁·沃特曼和大卫·帕特森把它画成了一张图，叫作屋顶线。

afefe2c6af42.en: Here is the roofline of one core of this computer, measured. <bookmark mark='a'/> The sloped part: the memory bandwidth, 18 gigabytes a second, the fastest we measured one core stream through main memory. A program on the slope is waiting for memory; the classic test, STREAM's triad, sits on or under it. <bookmark mark='b'/> The flat part: the fastest arithmetic we measured, 102 billion operations a second. They meet at the ridge, 5.5 operations per byte. <bookmark mark='c'/> A matrix times a vector does two operations per four-byte weight, and every weight is used once: it can't leave the slope. We measured at most 7.1 billion a second. <bookmark mark='d'/> A matrix times a matrix has intensity n over six. Watch it climb as n grows: at n of 32, overheads dominate and it manages 29; by 4096, it reaches 102, the roof.
afefe2c6af42.zh: 这是这台计算机一个核心的屋顶线，是实测出来的。<bookmark mark='a'/>斜的那段：内存带宽，每秒18GB，是我们测到的一个核心流式读写主存的最快速度。落在斜坡上的程序，是在等内存；经典的STREAM三元组测试，就落在斜坡上或斜坡下方。<bookmark mark='b'/>平的那段：我们测到的最快算术，每秒102千兆次运算。两段在拐点相遇，每字节5.5次运算。<bookmark mark='c'/>矩阵乘向量，每个四字节的权重做两次运算，而且每个权重只用一次：它离不开斜坡。我们测到的最多是每秒7.1千兆次。<bookmark mark='d'/>矩阵乘矩阵的算术强度是n除以6。看它随着n增大往上爬：n等于32时，开销占了主导，它只有29；到了4096，它达到102，碰到了屋顶。

6dc7b7a5ede4.en: Intensity is a property of the algorithm, but it only counts if the code earns it. <bookmark mark='a'/> All four matrix products of chapter five have the same intensity on paper, n over six, about 171 operations per byte. <bookmark mark='b'/> The textbook loop sits far below the roof, because it fetches its numbers over and over: its real intensity is far lower. <bookmark mark='c'/> Reordering and tiling climb towards the roof, <bookmark mark='d'/> and the library reaches it: 212 times higher, on the same line. The roofline says what's possible; the gap below it is the kernel writer's job. We also tried all 4 cores at once, but other jobs were using them, and the best we saw was 84: on a shared machine the roof you get is the roof you're left.
6dc7b7a5ede4.zh: 算术强度是算法的性质，但只有代码真正挣到它才算数。<bookmark mark='a'/>第5章的四种矩阵乘法，纸面上的算术强度都一样，n除以6，大约每字节171次运算。<bookmark mark='b'/>教科书循环远远落在屋顶下面，因为它一遍又一遍地取同样的数：它真正的算术强度要低得多。<bookmark mark='c'/>换序和分块往屋顶爬，<bookmark mark='d'/>而那个库碰到了屋顶：高了212倍，在同一条竖线上。屋顶线说的是可能达到什么；屋顶下面的那段差距，是写内核的人的活儿。我们也试了同时用全部4个核心，但别的任务正在用它们，我们看到的最好成绩是84：在一台共享的机器上，你能拿到的屋顶，就是别人留给你的屋顶。

6370ebb8c6cc.en: Now put a GPU on the same axes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our core's roofline is down in the corner. <bookmark mark='b'/> An H100's tensor cores do about 989 trillion operations a second in 16-bit arithmetic, and its memory moves 3.35 terabytes a second. Its ridge is at about 295 operations per byte. In 16-bit numbers, a square matrix product reaches it once n is about 890. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now the problem that Part 19 is about. A language model writing one token at a time multiplies every weight once: about one operation per byte. That's down on the slope, at 0.3 percent of the peak. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google's TPU paper of 2017 used exactly this picture. Their chip's ridge was at 1,350 operations per byte, a K80 GPU's at 9. Whether a chip is fast depends on where your program sits.
6370ebb8c6cc.zh: 现在把一块GPU放到同样的坐标轴上。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们那个核心的屋顶线，缩在左下角。<bookmark mark='b'/>H100的张量核心，在16位算术下每秒大约做989万亿次运算，它的内存每秒搬运3.35太字节。它的拐点在每字节大约295次运算。用16位数字，方阵乘法要在n大约到890时才能碰到它。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在说说第19部分要讲的问题。语言模型一次写一个词元，每个权重只乘一次：大约每字节一次运算。那是在斜坡的底部，只有峰值的0.3%。<bookmark mark='d'/>谷歌2017年的TPU论文，用的正是这张图。他们芯片的拐点在每字节1350次运算，K80 GPU的在9。一块芯片快不快，要看你的程序落在哪里。

fed26c1715a4.en: Chapter eight. Tensor cores and systolic arrays.
fed26c1715a4.zh: 第8章。张量核心与脉动阵列。

70f424f6f06e.en: There's an older idea that suits matrix products even better than a GPU's lanes. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1978 H. T. Kung and Charles Leiserson at Carnegie Mellon proposed systolic arrays: a grid of simple cells, each connected only to its neighbours, with data pulsing through in rhythm, like blood through the heart. <bookmark mark='b'/> A number read from memory enters at the edge and is used by every cell it passes, so the memory is read once while the arithmetic happens many times. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1982 Kung explained why it matters: for problems like matrix products, the operations per memory access can grow without asking for more bandwidth. The roofline's intensity, built into the wiring.
70f424f6f06e.zh: 有一个更老的想法，比GPU的通道还要适合矩阵乘法。<bookmark mark='a'/>1978年，卡内基梅隆大学的孔祥重和查尔斯·雷瑟尔森提出了脉动阵列：由简单单元组成的网格，每个单元只和邻居相连，数据有节奏地脉动着穿过它，就像血液穿过心脏。<bookmark mark='b'/>从内存读出的一个数，从边缘进入，被它经过的每个单元使用，所以内存只读一次，算术却做了很多次。<bookmark mark='c'/>1982年，孔祥重解释了为什么这很重要：对矩阵乘法这样的问题，每次访存的运算次数可以不断增长，而不需要更多带宽。这就是屋顶线里的算术强度，直接做进了连线里。

0c9b2c01f58f.en: Here's one computing a product, cycle by cycle, simulated. <bookmark mark='a'/> A four by four grid of cells, each holding a running sum. The rows of A come in from the left, the columns of B from the top, each one staggered a cycle behind the last. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every cycle, each cell multiplies the two numbers passing through it, adds the product to its sum, and hands the A number to the right and the B number down. <bookmark mark='c'/> Watch the active cells: a diagonal front sweeps across the grid. <bookmark mark='d'/> After 10 cycles every cell holds one entry of C. The result matches the product computed by numpy, exactly.
0c9b2c01f58f.zh: 这是一个正在计算乘积的阵列，一个周期一个周期地模拟出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个四乘四的单元网格，每个单元保存一个累加和。A的各行从左边进来，B的各列从上边进来，每一行、每一列都比前一个晚一个周期。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个周期，每个单元把穿过它的两个数相乘，加到自己的和上，再把A的数交给右边，把B的数交给下边。<bookmark mark='c'/>看那些正在工作的单元：一道斜的波前扫过整个网格。<bookmark mark='d'/>10个周期之后，每个单元都存着C的一个元素。结果和numpy算出的乘积完全一致。

9e58bd895b46.en: Why does it work? <bookmark mark='a'/> Because of the stagger, cell i, j meets a i k and b k j at cycle i plus j plus k: exactly the terms of its entry, each once. <bookmark mark='b'/> The last term reaches the far corner at cycle two n minus two plus K minus one, <bookmark mark='c'/> so the product takes K plus two n minus two cycles: ten for our example. <bookmark mark='d'/> And each number is read from memory once and used by n cells, so the memory traffic per operation falls like one over n. A bigger array is a bigger tile, with no cache needed: the reuse is in the wires.
9e58bd895b46.zh: 为什么这样行得通？<bookmark mark='a'/>因为错开了时间，单元i、j在第i加j加k个周期遇到a_ik和b_kj：正好是它那个元素的各项，每项一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>最后一项在第2n减2再加K减1个周期到达最远的角，<bookmark mark='c'/>所以整个乘积要K加2n减2个周期：我们的例子是十个。<bookmark mark='d'/>每个数从内存读一次，被n个单元使用，所以每次运算的访存量像n分之一那样下降。更大的阵列就是更大的块，而且不需要缓存：复用就在导线里。

07d2599af25a.en: In 2013 Google projected that if people used voice search for three minutes a day, the speech recognition networks alone would need twice its data centres. It built a chip instead, in fifteen months. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Tensor Processing Unit is a systolic array of 256 by 256 eight-bit multiply-adders, running at 700 megahertz: about 92 trillion operations a second. It was in Google's data centres from 2015, and it ran AlphaGo in its match against Lee Sedol. <bookmark mark='b'/> On Google's own workloads it was fifteen to thirty times faster than the CPU and GPU next to it, and thirty to eighty times better per watt. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price of a big fixed grid: work comes in whole tiles. A layer of 257 by 257 weights fills four tiles and uses a quarter of the cells. Shapes that are multiples of the array's size are the ones that run at full speed, on TPUs and GPUs alike.
07d2599af25a.zh: 2013年，谷歌估算，如果人们每天用三分钟语音搜索，光是语音识别网络，就需要把它的数据中心翻一倍。它转而造了一块芯片，只用了十五个月。<bookmark mark='a'/>张量处理器TPU，是一个256乘256的8位乘加器组成的脉动阵列，跑在700兆赫兹：每秒大约92万亿次运算。它从2015年起就在谷歌的数据中心里运行，还在和李世石的对局中运行了AlphaGo。<bookmark mark='b'/>在谷歌自己的工作负载上，它比旁边的CPU和GPU快十五到三十倍，每瓦性能好三十到八十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>一块大而固定的网格，代价是：工作要按整块来做。一层257乘257的权重，要占四块，只用上四分之一的单元。尺寸是阵列大小整数倍的形状，才能全速运行，在TPU上和GPU上都一样。

7cbe966f2171.en: GPUs took the hint in 2017. <bookmark mark='a'/> NVIDIA's Volta added tensor cores: units that take two four by four matrices and add their product to a third, all in one clock. Sixty-four multiply-adds per instruction, instead of one. <bookmark mark='b'/> A V100 has 640 of them, which gives its 125 trillion operations a second in half precision, eight times its ordinary lanes. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every generation since has made the tensor cores bigger and their numbers smaller: TF32 and bfloat16 in the A100, eight-bit floats in the H100, four-bit in Blackwell and in Rubin. The GPU is still a GPU, but most of its arithmetic now happens in small systolic engines inside it.
7cbe966f2171.zh: 2017年，GPU领会了这个意思。<bookmark mark='a'/>英伟达的Volta加入了张量核心：一种单元，在一个时钟里把两个四乘四矩阵相乘，再把乘积加到第三个上。每条指令六十四次乘加，而不是一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>一块V100有640个张量核心，由此得到半精度下每秒125万亿次运算，是它普通通道的八倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>此后的每一代，都让张量核心更大、用的数字更小：A100加入了TF32和bfloat16，H100是8位浮点，Blackwell和Rubin是4位。GPU还是GPU，但它的大部分算术，如今都发生在它内部那些小小的脉动引擎里。

1fede45c1bab.en: Chapter nine. Number formats in hardware.
1fede45c1bab.zh: 第9章。硬件里的数字格式。

aae7d0f1eb9f.en: A floating-point number is a sign, an exponent and a mantissa: scientific notation in base two. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is pi, rounded into each format the hardware of this part supports. <bookmark mark='b'/> FP32, the IEEE standard of 1985: eight exponent bits, twenty-three mantissa bits, about seven decimal digits. <bookmark mark='c'/> TF32 and bfloat16 keep FP32's eight-bit exponent, so the same range, but cut the mantissa to ten bits and to seven. FP16 trades the other way: five exponent bits, ten of mantissa. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then eight bits in two flavours, four exponent bits and three of mantissa, or five and two. <bookmark mark='e'/> And four bits: two of exponent, one of mantissa. Pi becomes three.
aae7d0f1eb9f.zh: 一个浮点数由符号、指数和尾数组成：二进制的科学计数法。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是π，被舍入到本部分的硬件所支持的每种格式里。<bookmark mark='b'/>FP32，1985年的IEEE标准：8个指数位，23个尾数位，大约七位十进制有效数字。<bookmark mark='c'/>TF32和bfloat16保留了FP32的8位指数，所以范围一样，但把尾数砍到了10位和7位。FP16反过来取舍：5个指数位，10个尾数位。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后是两种8位格式：4个指数位加3个尾数位，或者5个加2个。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有4位：2个指数位，1个尾数位。π变成了3。

7cb6fa285012.en: Two numbers describe a format. <bookmark mark='a'/> With M mantissa bits, each power of two is cut into two to the M equal steps. <bookmark mark='b'/> Rounding to the nearest value is off by at most half a step, so the relative error is at most two to the minus M plus one, the unit roundoff. That's precision. <bookmark mark='c'/> The exponent bits set the range: the largest number is just under two times two to the largest exponent. <bookmark mark='d'/> For E4M3 that's 448, because one bit pattern is kept to mean not-a-number. FP16 tops out at 65,504, which is why training in FP16 needs care, and bfloat16, with FP32's exponent, doesn't.
7cb6fa285012.zh: 两个数就能描述一种格式。<bookmark mark='a'/>有M个尾数位，每个2的幂之间就被切成2的M次方个相等的台阶。<bookmark mark='b'/>就近舍入，最多偏差半个台阶，所以相对误差至多是2的负M加1次方，叫作单位舍入误差。这就是精度。<bookmark mark='c'/>指数位决定范围：最大的数比2乘以2的最大指数次方略小一点。<bookmark mark='d'/>对E4M3来说是448，因为有一个位模式留着表示“非数”。FP16最大到65504，所以用FP16训练要小心，而有着FP32指数的bfloat16就不用。

120b80a47720.en: Let's measure it. Round a million Gaussian samples into each format and compare. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each step down in mantissa bits multiplies the error. FP32 is off by a few parts in a hundred million, bfloat16 by about 0.17 percent, eight-bit E4M3 by about 2.6 percent, and four bits by 14 percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> The white dots are the prediction: if the rounding error is spread evenly over a step, and values are spread evenly in the logarithm, the root-mean-square relative error is two to the minus M times a constant, the square root of log two over eighteen, about a fifth. The prediction ignores the very small and very large numbers, and the measurements land on it. Four bits miss it most: there, many samples fall below the smallest step.
120b80a47720.zh: 我们来测一测。把一百万个高斯样本舍入到每种格式，再做比较。<bookmark mark='a'/>尾数每少一位，误差就成倍增加。FP32的误差只有一亿分之几，bfloat16大约0.17%，8位的E4M3大约2.6%，4位是14%。<bookmark mark='b'/>白点是预测值：如果舍入误差在一个台阶里均匀分布，数值在对数上均匀分布，那么相对误差的均方根，就是2的负M次方乘以一个常数，即2的自然对数除以18再开平方，大约五分之一。这个预测忽略了极小和极大的数，测量值正好落在预测上。4位偏离得最多：在那里，很多样本落在了最小的台阶之下。

202684683678.en: Four bits have so little range that one scale for a whole matrix doesn't work: a few large values push everything else into the bottom step. <bookmark mark='a'/> The fix, standardized in 2023 by the Open Compute Project, is microscaling: give each block of thirty-two numbers its own shared exponent. <bookmark mark='b'/> We rounded a weight matrix of the voice model narrating this video each way. Sharing a scale per block of thirty-two cuts the four-bit error from 28 to 12 percent, and NVIDIA's finer blocks, with an eight-bit scale, to 9. <bookmark mark='c'/> Part 19 uses these formats to run a real model in four bits.
202684683678.zh: 4位的范围太小，整个矩阵用一个缩放因子是不行的：少数几个大值，会把其余的数全都挤到最底下那一级台阶里。<bookmark mark='a'/>解决办法在2023年由开放计算项目标准化，叫作微缩放：给每32个数一组，配一个共享的指数。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们把为这个视频配音的语音模型里的一个权重矩阵用每种方式都舍入了一遍。每32个数共享一个缩放因子，把4位的误差从28%降到了12%；英伟达更细的块，配上8位的缩放因子，又降到了9%。<bookmark mark='c'/>第19部分会用这些格式，以4位来运行一个真实的模型。

7db2da109c0c.en: Why go small at all? Because the multiplier's size grows roughly with the square of the mantissa's width, and every bit not moved is bandwidth saved. <bookmark mark='a'/> Halve the bits and the tensor cores do twice the work: an H100 does 989 trillion operations a second in bfloat16 and 1,979 in FP8; a Blackwell GPU doubles again in four bits. <bookmark mark='b'/> But only on hardware built for it. This computer's processor has no bfloat16 units, and PyTorch's bfloat16 product runs 3.9 times slower than its FP32. <bookmark mark='c'/> The history: Kahan's IEEE standard in 1985; bfloat16 from Google Brain for the TPU; eight-bit floats proposed by NVIDIA, Arm and Intel in 2022; microscaling in 2023. Part 18 trains in eight bits; Part 19 serves in four.
7db2da109c0c.zh: 到底为什么要用小格式？因为乘法器的大小，大致随尾数宽度的平方增长，而每少搬一位，就省下一份带宽。<bookmark mark='a'/>位数减半，张量核心就做两倍的工作：一块H100在bfloat16下每秒做989万亿次运算，在FP8下做1979万亿次；Blackwell GPU在4位下又翻一倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>但前提是硬件为它而造。这台计算机的处理器没有bfloat16单元，PyTorch的bfloat16矩阵乘法，比它的FP32慢3.9倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>历史是这样的：1985年卡亨主导的IEEE标准；谷歌大脑为TPU设计的bfloat16；2022年英伟达、Arm和英特尔提出的8位浮点；2023年的微缩放。第18部分用8位训练；第19部分用4位来推断。

9b3f01416fa5.en: A frontier model doesn't fit on one chip. <bookmark mark='a'/> Llama 3.1's 405 billion parameters take 810 gigabytes in sixteen-bit numbers; training, with gradients and the optimizer's state, needs about sixteen bytes per parameter, some 6.5 terabytes. An H100 holds eighty gigabytes, so at least 81 of them just to hold it, and Meta trained it on 16,384. <bookmark mark='b'/> So the chips have to talk, and every step away is slower. Inside the GPU, its memory: 3.35 terabytes a second. Between GPUs in one server, NVLink: 900 gigabytes a second. Between servers, an InfiniBand network: about a hundred. Each step costs about a factor of ten.
9b3f01416fa5.zh: 一个前沿模型，一块芯片是装不下的。<bookmark mark='a'/>Llama 3.1的4050亿个参数，用16位数存要810GB；训练时，加上梯度和优化器状态，每个参数大约要16个字节，总共约6.5太字节。一块H100装80GB，光是装下它，就至少要81块，而Meta是在16384块上训练的。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以芯片之间必须通信，而且每远一步就更慢。GPU内部，它自己的内存：每秒3.35太字节。同一台服务器里的GPU之间，NVLink：每秒900GB。服务器之间，InfiniBand网络：大约一百。每一步大约差十倍。

abb8a30d6248.en: NVIDIA built its own links. <bookmark mark='a'/> NVLink arrived with the P100 in 2016, 160 gigabytes a second per GPU; each generation since has roughly doubled it, to three terabytes a second for Rubin in 2026. <bookmark mark='b'/> Links need a shape. A switch connects everything to everything: NVIDIA's NVL72 racks put seventy-two GPUs on one NVLink fabric, 130 terabytes a second in all, 216 in the Rubin generation. <bookmark mark='c'/> Between racks, a fat tree, Charles Leiserson's design of 1985: more links higher up, so the top isn't a bottleneck. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google wires its TPUs in a three-dimensional torus, each chip linked to its six neighbours, and since TPU v4 reconfigures it with optical switches, 4,096 chips at a time.
abb8a30d6248.zh: 英伟达造了自己的链路。<bookmark mark='a'/>NVLink随P100在2016年问世，每块GPU每秒160GB；此后每一代大致翻一倍，到2026年的Rubin，是每秒三太字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>链路还需要一种拓扑形状。交换机把所有东西和所有东西连起来：英伟达的NVL72机柜，把72块GPU放在同一张NVLink网络上，总共每秒130太字节，Rubin这一代是216。<bookmark mark='c'/>机柜之间，用胖树，这是查尔斯·雷瑟尔森1985年的设计：越往上链路越多，顶层才不会成为瓶颈。<bookmark mark='d'/>谷歌把它的TPU连成三维环面，每块芯片连着六个邻居；从TPU v4起，还用光路交换机重新配置它，一次4096块芯片。

8356ca638373.en: To reason about communication, use the simplest model that works. <bookmark mark='a'/> Sending a message of n bytes costs a fixed alpha, the latency, plus n over beta, the bandwidth. <bookmark mark='b'/> We measured it between two processes on this computer, passing messages from eight bytes to thirty-two megabytes. <bookmark mark='c'/> The fit: alpha about 14 microseconds, beta about 3.3 gigabytes a second. <bookmark mark='d'/> Below alpha times beta, about 50 kilobytes here, a message costs the same whatever its size; above it, bandwidth is everything. On a GPU cluster the numbers change, microseconds and hundreds of gigabytes a second, but the shape doesn't.
8356ca638373.zh: 要分析通信，就用最简单而管用的模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>发一条n字节的消息，花一个固定的α，也就是延迟，再加上n除以β，β是带宽。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们在这台计算机的两个进程之间测了它，消息从8字节到32兆字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>拟合结果：α大约14微秒，β大约每秒3.3GB。<bookmark mark='d'/>小于α乘β，在这里大约50千字节，消息不管多大，代价都差不多；大于它，带宽就决定一切。在GPU集群上，数字会变，是微秒和每秒几百GB，但形状不变。

19d6f2fde596.en: Training on many GPUs means, every step, adding up everyone's gradients so that all of them get the total: an all-reduce. <bookmark mark='a'/> The ring algorithm splits each GPU's data into p chunks. <bookmark mark='b'/> In each step, every GPU sends one chunk to its neighbour and adds the chunk it receives to its own. After p minus one steps, each GPU holds one chunk of the full sum. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then p minus one more steps pass the finished chunks around, until every GPU has all of them. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each step sends n over p bytes, so the total time is two times p minus one alphas, plus two times p minus one over p, times n over beta. The bandwidth term never exceeds two n over beta, however many GPUs there are, and no algorithm can do better on it. Part 18 builds data parallelism on this.
19d6f2fde596.zh: 在许多块GPU上训练，意味着每一步都要把所有人的梯度加起来，让每块GPU都拿到总和：这叫全规约。<bookmark mark='a'/>环形算法把每块GPU的数据切成p块。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一步，每块GPU把一块发给邻居，再把收到的那块加到自己的上面。p减1步之后，每块GPU都持有完整总和的一块。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后再用p减1步，把算完的块传一圈，直到每块GPU都拿到全部。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一步发送n除以p个字节，所以总时间是2乘以p减1个α，加上2乘以p分之p减1，再乘以n除以β。不管有多少块GPU，带宽项都不超过2n除以β，而且在这一项上，没有哪种算法能做得更好。第18部分的数据并行，就建立在这上面。

135ea410772d.en: There's another way: a tree. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add pairs, then pairs of pairs, up to one GPU, and send the total back down. That's two log p steps instead of two p, but each step sends the whole message. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are both, in units of the latency, for eight, sixty-four and 512 GPUs. For small messages the tree wins: fewer steps. For large ones the ring wins: less data per step. <bookmark mark='c'/> With 512 GPUs the crossover is near 63 alpha beta. With a few microseconds of latency and NVLink's bandwidth, alpha beta is a few megabytes, and gradients are gigabytes: rings for bulk data, trees for latency, and libraries like NVIDIA's NCCL choose for you. <bookmark mark='d'/> We also timed both on four processes of this computer, but with every core shared with other jobs, the measurements ran several times slower than the model and too noisy to check it: the model describes a network, not a busy operating system.
135ea410772d.zh: 还有另一种办法：树。<bookmark mark='a'/>先两两相加，再把两对相加，一直加到一块GPU上，再把总和发回去。这是2乘log p步，而不是2p步，但每一步都要发送整条消息。<bookmark mark='b'/>这里是两种算法，以延迟为单位，分别对8块、64块和512块GPU。消息小的时候，树赢：步数少。消息大的时候，环赢：每一步的数据少。<bookmark mark='c'/>512块GPU时，交叉点在大约63倍的α乘β。延迟几微秒、带宽是NVLink那么大时，α乘β是几兆字节，而梯度是吉字节量级：大块数据用环，看重延迟用树，像英伟达NCCL这样的库会替你选。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们也在这台计算机的四个进程上给两种算法计了时，但每个核心都和别的任务共用，测出来的时间比模型慢好几倍，噪声也太大，没法用来检验它：这个模型描述的是网络，而不是一个忙碌的操作系统。

1c3c3cb2ee46.en: Here is chapter five's tiling, written for a GPU, the way textbooks teach it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each block of threads computes one T by T tile of C, one thread per entry. <bookmark mark='b'/> The block declares two tiles of shared memory, the programmer-managed SRAM of chapter six. <bookmark mark='c'/> In each round, every thread copies one number of A and one of B from global memory into the shared tiles: neighbouring threads, neighbouring addresses, coalesced. <bookmark mark='d'/> The threads wait for each other, then each does T multiply-adds out of shared memory, and waits again before the tiles are overwritten. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every number fetched from global memory is used T times: the intensity is T over four. With tiles of thirty-two, that's eight operations per byte, still below an H100's ridge. Real kernels go further: each thread keeps a small tile of its own in registers, and the multiply-adds go to the tensor cores.
1c3c3cb2ee46.zh: 这是第5章的分块，照教科书的教法，写成GPU代码。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个线程块计算C的一个T乘T的块，每个线程负责一个元素。<bookmark mark='b'/>线程块声明两个共享内存块，也就是第6章里由程序员管理的SRAM。<bookmark mark='c'/>每一轮，每个线程从全局内存里拷贝A的一个数和B的一个数到共享块里：相邻的线程，相邻的地址，访存合并。<bookmark mark='d'/>线程们互相等待，然后每个线程从共享内存里做T次乘加，再等一次，然后这些块才会被覆盖。<bookmark mark='e'/>每个从全局内存取来的数被用了T次：算术强度是T除以4。块大小取32，就是每字节8次运算，仍然低于H100的拐点。真正的内核会更进一步：每个线程在寄存器里再保留一小块自己的数据，乘加交给张量核心去做。

95ce1ddceaea.en: How many threads can share a multiprocessor? Chapter three said: as many as it takes to hide memory's latency. But they share its registers and its shared memory. <bookmark mark='a'/> An H100's multiprocessor has 65,536 registers. A kernel whose threads each need R registers can keep at most 65,536 over thirty-two R warps resident, and never more than sixty-four. The fraction is called occupancy. <bookmark mark='b'/> It falls in steps as each thread grows. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our tile kernel, small and simple, runs at 100 percent. A kernel with big register tiles, the kind that feeds tensor cores, at 25. <bookmark mark='d'/> And that can be faster: in 2010 Vasily Volkov showed that fewer threads, each doing more work from its registers, often beat full occupancy. It's chapter three's trade again: hide latency with threads, or with more arithmetic per load.
95ce1ddceaea.zh: 一个多处理器能容纳多少线程？第3章说：要多少，就要多到足以隐藏内存延迟。但它们共用多处理器的寄存器和共享内存。<bookmark mark='a'/>H100的一个多处理器有65536个寄存器。如果一个内核的每个线程要R个寄存器，那最多只能驻留65536除以32R个线程束，而且永远不超过64个。这个比例叫占用率。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个线程越大，它就一级一级地往下掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们那个小而简单的分块内核，占用率是100%。一个用大寄存器块、专门喂张量核心的内核，只有25%。<bookmark mark='d'/>而后者可能更快：2010年，瓦西里·沃尔科夫证明，更少的线程、每个线程用寄存器做更多的事，常常胜过满占用率。这又是第3章的那个权衡：用线程来隐藏延迟，还是用每次读取做更多算术来隐藏。

15971b027352.en: Writing kernels like that by hand is hard, and getting the last factor of two is harder. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2019 Philippe Tillet, a graduate student at Harvard, published Triton with H. T. Kung, the Kung of the systolic arrays, and David Cox. You write Python, and you program a block of the output, not a thread. <bookmark mark='b'/> Load a tile of A, a tile of B, multiply them with one dot, accumulate, move on: the tiling of chapter five, in eleven lines. The compiler decides how the threads share the work, stages the tiles through shared memory, coalesces the loads and uses the tensor cores. <bookmark mark='c'/> OpenAI released it in 2021, and PyTorch's compiler now writes Triton kernels itself. NVIDIA's CUTLASS library and JAX's Pallas play the same role in C plus plus and in JAX.
15971b027352.zh: 这样手写内核很难，挤出最后那两倍性能就更难。<bookmark mark='a'/>2019年，哈佛的研究生菲利普·蒂莱，和孔祥重，也就是做脉动阵列的那位孔祥重，以及大卫·考克斯一起发表了Triton。你写的是Python，编程的对象是输出的一个块，而不是一个线程。<bookmark mark='b'/>取A的一块、B的一块，用一个点积把它们相乘，累加，往下走：第5章的分块，十一行代码。编译器决定线程怎样分工，把块经由共享内存中转，合并访存，并用上张量核心。<bookmark mark='c'/>OpenAI在2021年发布了它，如今PyTorch的编译器自己就会写Triton内核。英伟达的CUTLASS库和JAX的Pallas，在C加加和JAX里扮演同样的角色。

5a23e553e00a.en: The model example of thinking this way is FlashAttention. <bookmark mark='a'/> Attention computes a score for every pair of positions: a T by T table. The standard implementation writes that table out to high-bandwidth memory, then reads it back for the softmax, then again to weight the values. For long inputs that traffic dominates, while the tensor cores wait. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2022 Tri Dao and colleagues at Stanford computed attention tile by tile instead, keeping each tile in on-chip SRAM, with a running maximum and sum so the softmax comes out exact. <bookmark mark='c'/> The table is never written out at all. They proved its memory traffic is T squared d squared over M, M the SRAM size: less than the standard version's whenever d squared is smaller than M, as it is in practice. The same arithmetic, faster, because it moves fewer bytes. Part 19 derives it.
5a23e553e00a.zh: 这种思路的典范，是FlashAttention。<bookmark mark='a'/>注意力要给每一对位置算一个分数：一张T乘T的表。标准实现把这张表写到高带宽内存里，再读回来做softmax，然后再读一次去给值加权。输入一长，这些搬运就占了主导，张量核心只能干等。<bookmark mark='b'/>2022年，斯坦福的道三（Tri Dao）和同事改成一块一块地计算注意力，每一块都留在片上SRAM里，用一个滚动的最大值和滚动的和，让softmax的结果精确无误。<bookmark mark='c'/>这张表根本不写出去。他们证明，它的访存量是T平方乘d平方除以M，M是SRAM的大小：只要d平方小于M，就比标准版本少，而实践中正是如此。同样的算术，更快，因为它搬的字节更少。第19部分会推导它。

c95fce4fb735.en: Chapter twelve. FLOPs, dollars and watts.

82dbc5e9fbe3.en: How fast is all this improving? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are the flagship accelerators of NVIDIA, Google, AMD and Amazon since 2017, from Epoch AI's database. Their sixteen-bit tensor arithmetic doubled every 1.8 years. <bookmark mark='b'/> Their memory bandwidth doubled every 2.6. <bookmark mark='c'/> Arithmetic is outrunning memory. Epoch's own study of forty-seven accelerators found the same, 2.3 years against four, and Amir Gholami and colleagues, looking back twenty years, called it the memory wall. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the ridge of the roofline keeps moving right: in this data the operations a chip can do per byte it reads doubled every 5.5 years. Each generation needs more reuse to stay busy.
82dbc5e9fbe3.zh: 这一切进步得有多快？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是英伟达、谷歌、AMD和亚马逊从2017年以来的旗舰加速器，来自Epoch AI的数据库。它们的16位张量算力，每1.8年翻一倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>内存带宽，每2.6年翻一倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>算术跑得比内存快。Epoch自己对47款加速器的研究也发现了同样的事，2.3年对4年；阿米尔·戈拉米和同事回顾了二十年，把它叫作内存墙。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以屋顶线的拐点一直往右移：在这组数据里，一块芯片每读一个字节能做的运算次数，每5.5年翻一倍。每一代都需要更多的复用，才能保持忙碌。

13f6b839a867.en: Here's the ridge, generation by generation, from the datasheets. <bookmark mark='a'/> In sixteen-bit numbers it moved from about 139 operations per byte for a V100 to about 312 for a Blackwell GPU. <bookmark mark='b'/> But each generation also added a smaller format, and in its smallest format the ridge has climbed to about 1,823 for Rubin. Smaller numbers do double duty: twice the arithmetic per cycle, and half the bytes per number, which is what brings a workload back up to the ridge.
13f6b839a867.zh: 这是一代一代的拐点，来自各家的数据手册。<bookmark mark='a'/>用16位数字，它从V100的每字节大约139次运算，移到了Blackwell GPU的大约312次。<bookmark mark='b'/>但每一代也加入了更小的格式，用各自最小的格式算，Rubin的拐点已经爬到了大约1823。更小的数字身兼两职：每个周期两倍的算术，每个数一半的字节，正是后者把工作负载拉回到拐点上。

f90d7e82465b.en: What about energy? <bookmark mark='a'/> Divide each chip's peak by its power: sixteen-bit operations per second per watt doubled every 2.9 years in this data; Epoch found three. <bookmark mark='b'/> The graphics card AlexNet trained on spent about 154 picojoules per floating-point operation. An H100 spends about 0.7: about 220 times less, partly by using fewer bits. Chapter six's lesson still holds, though: fetching the operands from memory costs more than the arithmetic. Price-performance, by Epoch's count, doubles about every two years.
f90d7e82465b.zh: 那能量呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>用每块芯片的峰值除以它的功耗：在这组数据里，每瓦每秒的16位运算次数，每2.9年翻一倍；Epoch算出来是三年。<bookmark mark='b'/>训练AlexNet的那块显卡，每次浮点运算大约花154皮焦。一块H100大约花0.7：少了大约220倍，部分是因为用了更少的位。不过第6章的教训仍然成立：把操作数从内存里取出来，比算术本身更费能。按Epoch的统计，性价比大约每两年翻一倍。

678c0f92d30d.en: And then there's the electricity. <bookmark mark='a'/> The International Energy Agency estimated that data centres used about 415 terawatt-hours in 2024, about one and a half percent of the world's electricity, and projected about 945 by 2030, with AI the main driver. <bookmark mark='b'/> Training Llama 3.1 took a cluster drawing an estimated twenty-odd megawatts. <bookmark mark='c'/> NVIDIA now describes its Rubin systems in units of a hundred-megawatt AI factory: forty thousand GPUs, about 2.5 kilowatts each once cooling and networking are counted. The constraint on building AI is increasingly the power line.
678c0f92d30d.zh: 然后还有电力。<bookmark mark='a'/>国际能源署估计，2024年数据中心用了大约415太瓦时，约占全世界电力的百分之一点五，并预计到2030年约为945，人工智能是主要推动力。<bookmark mark='b'/>训练Llama 3.1的集群，估计要二十多兆瓦。<bookmark mark='c'/>英伟达现在用一百兆瓦的“AI工厂”来描述它的Rubin系统：四万块GPU，算上冷却和网络，每块大约2.5千瓦。建设人工智能的瓶颈，越来越是那根电线。

4367aa62319b.en: The TPU was the first of many chips built only for neural networks. <bookmark mark='a'/> Google's line went from an eight-bit inference chip in 2015 to training: the TPU v2 in 2017 added high-bandwidth memory, bfloat16 and pods of chips wired together; v4 linked 4,096 of them through optical switches. <bookmark mark='b'/> The seventh generation, Ironwood, in 2025: 4,614 trillion eight-bit operations a second per chip, in pods of 9,216. <bookmark mark='c'/> And in April 2026 Google announced two eighth-generation chips, one for training and one for serving, with training superpods of 9,600 chips. Google trains its Gemini models on its own TPUs. <bookmark mark='d'/> Amazon builds Trainium, Microsoft Maia, Meta MTIA. Most are systolic arrays of some size, fed by high-bandwidth memory: the recipe of chapters six to eight.
4367aa62319b.zh: TPU是众多只为神经网络而造的芯片里的第一款。<bookmark mark='a'/>谷歌这条产品线，从2015年的一块8位推断芯片，走向了训练：2017年的TPU v2加入了高带宽内存、bfloat16，以及由许多芯片连成的集群；v4用光路交换机把4096块连在一起。<bookmark mark='b'/>第七代Ironwood，2025年：每块芯片每秒4614万亿次8位运算，集群规模9216块。<bookmark mark='c'/>2026年4月，谷歌发布了两款第八代芯片，一款用于训练，一款用于推断服务，训练超级集群有9600块芯片。谷歌就在自己的TPU上训练Gemini模型。<bookmark mark='d'/>亚马逊造Trainium，微软造Maia，Meta造MTIA。它们大多是某种规模的脉动阵列，由高带宽内存喂数据：正是第6到第8章的配方。

7a225a3df27f.en: Others changed the shape of the chip itself. <bookmark mark='a'/> Chips are cut from a silicon wafer thirty centimetres across. Cerebras doesn't cut it: the whole wafer is one chip. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its third version, from 2024, has four trillion transistors, nine hundred thousand cores, and forty-four gigabytes of SRAM spread among them, so a model's weights can sit next to the arithmetic instead of in memory chips off to the side. <bookmark mark='c'/> It's about fifty-seven times the area of an H100's die. The hard parts were the ones everyone said were impossible: defects on a wafer that size, which it routes around, and cooling and powering it.
7a225a3df27f.zh: 还有人改变了芯片本身的形状。<bookmark mark='a'/>芯片是从直径三十厘米的硅晶圆上切下来的。Cerebras不切：整片晶圆就是一块芯片。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的第三代产品是2024年的，有四万亿个晶体管、九十万个核心，以及分布在它们之间的44GB SRAM，所以模型的权重可以就挨着运算单元，而不是放在旁边的内存芯片里。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的面积大约是H100裸片的五十七倍。难点正是大家都说不可能的那些：这么大一片晶圆上的缺陷，它要绕开走；还有给它散热和供电。

8ca9366d00ba.en: Groq took the opposite bet from the GPU. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its founder, Jonathan Ross, had helped start the TPU project at Google. Groq's LPU has no high-bandwidth memory at all: the weights live in on-chip SRAM, and the compiler schedules every cycle in advance, so nothing waits on a cache. <bookmark mark='b'/> For writing one token at a time, the roofline's slope is everything, and SRAM is fast. In December 2025 NVIDIA licensed Groq's technology and hired its founders, and in March 2026 it described the result: a rack of 256 Groq 3 LPUs, each with about 156 terabytes a second of SRAM bandwidth, against 19.2 for a Rubin GPU's memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price is capacity: 500 megabytes per chip. A trillion-parameter model in four bits needs about 1,000 of them. So NVIDIA pairs them: GPUs read the long prompt and keep the attention; LPUs run the rest of each new token.
8ca9366d00ba.zh: Groq押了和GPU相反的注。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的创始人乔纳森·罗斯，曾在谷歌参与发起TPU项目。Groq的LPU根本没有高带宽内存：权重住在片上SRAM里，编译器预先安排好每一个周期，所以没有什么要等缓存。<bookmark mark='b'/>对一次写一个词元来说，屋顶线的斜坡就是一切，而SRAM很快。2025年12月，英伟达获得了Groq技术的授权，并聘请了它的创始人；2026年3月，它介绍了成果：一个装有256块Groq 3 LPU的机柜，每块的SRAM带宽大约每秒156太字节，而Rubin GPU的内存是19.2。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是容量：每块芯片500兆字节。一个一万亿参数的模型，用4位存，大约需要1000块。所以英伟达把它们搭配起来用：GPU读长长的提示，负责注意力；LPU运行每个新词元的其余部分。

8d477a9140f6.en: Two older dreams are still being chased. <bookmark mark='a'/> Analog computing in memory: store each weight as the conductance of a cell in a grid, apply the inputs as voltages on the rows, and by Ohm's law each cell's current is a product; by Kirchhoff's law the currents on a column add up. <bookmark mark='b'/> A whole matrix-vector product in one step, with no weights moved at all. In 2023 IBM ran speech recognition on a chip with thirty-five million such cells; the hard parts are noise and precision. <bookmark mark='c'/> And neuromorphic chips compute with spikes, like neurons, and only when something changes: IBM's TrueNorth in 2014, Intel's Loihi, and in 2024 Hala Point, with over a billion artificial neurons. Neither runs today's frontier models. Both are bets on chapter six's lesson: the cheapest data movement is none.
8d477a9140f6.zh: 还有两个更老的梦想，人们仍在追逐。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个是模拟存内计算：把每个权重存成网格里一个单元的电导，把输入作为电压加在各行上，按欧姆定律，每个单元的电流就是一个乘积；按基尔霍夫定律，一列上的电流自动相加。<bookmark mark='b'/>一整个矩阵乘向量，一步完成，一个权重都不用搬。2023年，IBM在一块有三千五百万个这种单元的芯片上运行了语音识别；难点在于噪声和精度。<bookmark mark='c'/>另一个是类脑芯片，它们像神经元一样用脉冲计算，而且只在有变化时才计算：2014年IBM的TrueNorth，英特尔的Loihi，以及2024年的Hala Point，有超过十亿个人工神经元。两者都还跑不了今天的前沿模型。它们押的都是第6章的那个教训：最便宜的数据搬运，就是不搬。

017a3ed5ceea.zh: 第14章。前沿：2026年底的计算机。

abaf4b5d897b.en: Where does all this stand at the end of 2026? <bookmark mark='a'/> NVIDIA's Blackwell, announced in March 2024, hit the limit of chipmaking: a die can't be larger than the area a lithography machine exposes at once. So Blackwell is two dies at that limit, joined by ten terabytes a second so they act as one GPU: 208 billion transistors, with tensor cores for four-bit numbers. <bookmark mark='b'/> The unit of sale became the rack. A GB200 NVL72 puts seventy-two of them on one NVLink fabric, liquid cooled, so that the rack behaves like one enormous GPU, and the 2025 Blackwell Ultra raised the memory to 288 gigabytes per GPU.
abaf4b5d897b.zh: 到2026年底，这一切走到了哪里？<bookmark mark='a'/>英伟达2024年3月发布的Blackwell，碰到了芯片制造的极限：一块裸片不能比光刻机一次曝光的面积更大。所以Blackwell是两块达到这个极限的裸片，以每秒十太字节连在一起，像一块GPU一样工作：2080亿个晶体管，张量核心支持4位数字。<bookmark mark='b'/>销售的单位变成了机柜。一台GB200 NVL72把72块这样的GPU放在同一张NVLink网络上，用液体冷却，让整个机柜表现得像一块巨大的GPU；2025年的Blackwell Ultra又把每块GPU的内存提高到288GB。

60d3f81f5c53.en: Its successor is in production now. <bookmark mark='a'/> A Vera Rubin NVL72 rack holds seventy-two Rubin GPUs and thirty-six of NVIDIA's own Arm CPUs. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each GPU has 288 gigabytes of the fourth generation of high-bandwidth memory, read at 19.2 terabytes a second, and does 35 quadrillion four-bit operations a second for training. The sixth NVLink moves 3 terabytes a second per GPU, 216 across the rack. <bookmark mark='c'/> NVIDIA now sells these by the hundred megawatts: forty thousand GPUs in one building. <bookmark mark='d'/> And note the ridge: about 1,823 operations per byte in four-bit arithmetic. Only work with enormous reuse can use all of it.
60d3f81f5c53.zh: 它的后继者现在已经投产。<bookmark mark='a'/>一台Vera Rubin NVL72机柜里，有72块Rubin GPU，和36块英伟达自己的Arm CPU。<bookmark mark='b'/>每块GPU有288GB的第四代高带宽内存，每秒读19.2太字节，训练时每秒做35千万亿次4位运算。第六代NVLink每块GPU每秒搬运3太字节，整个机柜216太字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>英伟达现在按一百兆瓦来卖这些东西：一栋楼里四万块GPU。<bookmark mark='d'/>再注意一下拐点：用4位算术，大约每字节1823次运算。只有复用极多的工作，才能把它全部用上。

a615df2d4ed4.en: The unit of computing keeps growing. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2022 the GPUs that shared a fast fabric were the eight in one server. <bookmark mark='b'/> With Blackwell, seventy-two in a rack. <bookmark mark='c'/> Google's torus pods were larger still: 4,096 TPU v4 chips, 9,216 Ironwood chips in 2025, and 9,600 in a TPU 8t superpod announced this year. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google says its new data-centre network can make a million of them work as one cluster. Part 18 is about what it takes to use machines like these for a single training run.
a615df2d4ed4.zh: 计算的单位还在不断变大。<bookmark mark='a'/>2022年，共享同一张高速网络的GPU，是一台服务器里的八块。<bookmark mark='b'/>到了Blackwell，是一个机柜里的七十二块。<bookmark mark='c'/>谷歌的环面集群还要更大：4096块TPU v4芯片，2025年9216块Ironwood芯片，以及今年发布的TPU 8t超级集群里的9600块。<bookmark mark='d'/>谷歌说，它新的数据中心网络，能让一百万块这样的芯片像一个集群那样工作。第18部分要讲的，就是怎样用这样的机器完成一次训练。

cd294e8dc226.en: The newest trend is to split the work by where it sits on the roofline. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reading a prompt multiplies matrices by matrices: high intensity, arithmetic-bound. Writing the answer, one token at a time, multiplies matrices by vectors: low intensity, memory-bound. <bookmark mark='b'/> So NVIDIA pairs Rubin GPUs, and a variant for very long prompts, with Groq's SRAM chips for decoding; <bookmark mark='c'/> and Google's eighth generation is two chips, one for training and one for serving, with three times its predecessor's on-chip memory for the attention cache. <bookmark mark='d'/> The limits now are power, memory bandwidth and the links between chips, the three threads of this part.
cd294e8dc226.zh: 最新的趋势，是按工作落在屋顶线上的位置来拆分它。<bookmark mark='a'/>读一个提示，是矩阵乘矩阵：算术强度高，受算力限制。一次一个词元地写答案，是矩阵乘向量：算术强度低，受内存限制。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以英伟达把Rubin GPU，以及一款专为超长提示设计的变体，和Groq的SRAM芯片搭配起来做解码；<bookmark mark='c'/>谷歌的第八代是两块芯片，一块用于训练，一块用于推断服务，片上内存是前一代的三倍，用来存注意力缓存。<bookmark mark='d'/>如今的限制是功耗、内存带宽，以及芯片之间的链路，正是本部分的三条主线。

dcfa08953cc3.en: Let's take stock. When the voltage stopped falling, clocks stopped rising, and the only way to use more transistors was in parallel. GPUs run thousands of threads in warps, and pay for divergence. Matrix multiplication is nearly all of a network's arithmetic, and tiling lets each number fetched be used many times. Memory is a hierarchy, small and close to large and far, and the roofline says whether a program is bound by arithmetic or by bytes. Systolic arrays build reuse into the wiring. Fewer bits buy throughput at a measured cost in error. And when one chip isn't enough, a ring all-reduce shares the work at nearly the bandwidth limit.
dcfa08953cc3.zh: 我们来总结一下。电压降不下去以后，时钟就不再上涨，用上更多晶体管的唯一办法，就是并行。GPU以线程束为单位运行成千上万个线程，并为分支发散付出代价。矩阵乘法几乎就是一个网络全部的算术，分块让每个取来的数被用上很多次。内存是一个层次，从小而近到大而远，屋顶线告诉你，一个程序受限于算术还是受限于字节。脉动阵列把复用做进了连线里。更少的位数换来了吞吐量，误差的代价可以测量。一块芯片不够时，环形全规约以接近带宽极限的效率分担工作。

f0af29c24857.en: All of this comes back. Part 18 trains a model across many GPUs, with the alpha-beta model, the ring all-reduce and eight-bit arithmetic. Part 19 puts inference on the roofline: reading a prompt is arithmetic-bound, writing an answer is memory-bound, and FlashAttention and four-bit formats follow. Part 15's memory methods are sized to high-bandwidth memory and written to use the tensor cores, and Part 16's experts trade tokens across an NVLink domain, while the tensor cores' two-in-four sparsity doubles their arithmetic.
f0af29c24857.zh: 这些都会再出现。第18部分在许多GPU上训练模型，用到α–β模型、环形全规约，以及8位算术。第19部分把推断放到屋顶线上：读提示受算力限制，写答案受内存限制，FlashAttention和4位格式随之而来。第15部分的记忆方法，是按高带宽内存的大小设计、为了用上张量核心而写的；第16部分的专家在NVLink域里交换词元，而张量核心的四选二稀疏，能让它们的算术翻倍。

d962ba8121b3.en: Here are six problems to try, from arithmetic intensity to the latency a GPU has to hide. Pause here, and work through them; full solutions are in this part's notes.
d962ba8121b3.zh: 这里有六道习题，从算术强度，一直到GPU要隐藏的延迟。请在这里暂停，动手做一做；完整的解答在本部分的笔记里。

dd8e8916717b.en: Next time: pretraining at scale. Where the trillions of tokens come from and how they're cleaned; how one model is cut across thousands of GPUs, by data, by tensor, by pipeline stage and by expert, with this part's all-reduce at the centre; how training in eight bits stays stable; and what goes wrong on a run of sixteen thousand GPUs.
dd8e8916717b.zh: 下一次：大规模预训练。上万亿个词元从哪里来，又怎样清洗；一个模型怎样被切开，分到成千上万块GPU上，按数据、按张量、按流水线阶段、按专家，而本部分的全规约就在正中央；8位训练怎样保持稳定；以及在一万六千块GPU上训练时，会出什么问题。

124e9a98468b.en: Hennessy and Patterson's book is the place to go deeper on all of this, and Kirk and Hwu's on GPU programming. Thanks for watching, and see you in Part 18.
124e9a98468b.zh: 想深入了解这一切，就去读亨尼西和帕特森的书；GPU编程，就读柯克和胡文美的书。感谢观看，第18部分再见。
